units.title: What AI Is
units.tip: Artificial intelligence is software that can learn from data and make decisions without being explicitly programmed for every case. Machine learning is a subset of AI that learns patterns from data. Deep learning uses neural networks inspired by how brains work.

exercises.question: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?
exercises.answer: Software that can learn and make decisions from data
exercises.explain: AI systems learn patterns from data and use those patterns to make predictions or decisions. This differs from traditional programs which follow hard-coded rules.
choices: A computer that moves on its own
Software that can learn and make decisions from data
A robot with human-like feelings
Any computer program

exercises.question: What is the difference between AI and machine learning?
exercises.answer: AI is the broad field; machine learning is a technique within it
exercises.explain: Artificial intelligence is the overall goal of making machines intelligent. Machine learning is one approach to achieve that by learning from data.
choices: They are the same thing
AI is the broad field; machine learning is a technique within it
Machine learning is older
AI can only run on special hardware

exercises.question: What is deep learning?
exercises.answer: Machine learning using neural networks with many layers
exercises.explain: Deep learning uses artificial neural networks with multiple layers to process data. The 'deep' refers to the depth of these layered networks.
choices: Learning by reading books
Machine learning using neural networks with many layers
Any AI system that works well
A philosophy about understanding

exercises.question: What do all AI systems have in common?
exercises.answer: They use data and algorithms to solve problems
exercises.explain: Whether supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement learning, AI systems process data with algorithms to find patterns and make predictions.
choices: They all use neural networks
They use data and algorithms to solve problems
They must always be accurate
They need human approval for every decision

exercises.question: What is a simple example of artificial intelligence?
exercises.answer: Email spam filtering that learns what is spam
exercises.explain: Spam filters learn from examples of spam and legitimate emails to classify new incoming mail. This is AI learning from data.
choices: A calculator
A video game with fixed rules
Email spam filtering that learns what is spam
A digital clock

exercises.question: Which statement best describes narrow AI?
exercises.answer: AI designed to excel at one specific task
exercises.explain: Narrow AI (also called weak AI) is built to do one thing very well, like play chess or recognize images. Most AI today is narrow AI.
choices: AI that only works for children
AI designed to excel at one specific task
AI that cannot make mistakes
AI that learns while it is running

exercises.question: What would general AI (AGI) be able to do?
exercises.answer: Learn and solve any intellectual task a human can
exercises.explain: General artificial intelligence would be as intelligent as a human and able to learn and solve any type of problem. It does not exist yet.
choices: Only answer questions about one topic
Learn and solve any intellectual task a human can
Think and feel like a human
Replace all jobs immediately

exercises.question: How do machine learning and deep learning differ in complexity?
exercises.answer: Deep learning uses more layers and processes more complex data
exercises.explain: Deep learning uses multi-layered neural networks that can process complex, unstructured data like images and text more effectively than simpler ML algorithms.
choices: Deep learning is always faster
Deep learning uses more layers and processes more complex data
Machine learning is only for experts
Deep learning never requires training data

exercises.question: What makes supervised learning different from unsupervised learning?
exercises.answer: Supervised learning uses labeled training data with correct answers
exercises.explain: Supervised learning trains on data with labels (correct answers). Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data without knowing what it is looking for.
choices: Supervised learning is always better
Supervised learning uses labeled training data with correct answers
Unsupervised learning requires a teacher
Supervised learning cannot use large datasets

exercises.question: Why might a company choose machine learning over traditional programming?
exercises.answer: Because the pattern is too complex or changes over time
exercises.explain: Machine learning shines when the rules are hard to code by hand or need to adapt to new data. Traditional programming works when rules are clear and fixed.
choices: Because machine learning is always cheaper
Because the pattern is too complex or changes over time
Because it requires no training data
Because it is guaranteed to be error-free

units.title: How Machines Learn
units.tip: Machines learn by adjusting internal weights to minimize errors on training data. In supervised learning, we provide examples with correct answers. In unsupervised learning, the machine finds its own patterns. Overfitting happens when a model memorizes data instead of learning general rules.

exercises.question: What is training data in machine learning?
exercises.answer: Examples the system learns from to find patterns
exercises.explain: Training data is the set of examples used to teach an AI system. The system analyzes this data to learn patterns it can apply to new, unseen data.
choices: Data the system will never see
Examples the system learns from to find patterns
Incorrect data used to test the system
Data stored in a database

exercises.question: Why is more training data usually better for machine learning?
exercises.answer: More examples help the system learn more robust patterns
exercises.explain: Larger, diverse training datasets help AI systems find general patterns rather than memorizing specific examples. More data reduces overfitting.
choices: Because it makes training faster
More examples help the system learn more robust patterns
Because bigger data is always better quality
To make the system forget old patterns

exercises.question: What does it mean to 'train' a machine learning model?
exercises.answer: Adjust internal parameters to fit patterns in the data
exercises.explain: Training means feeding data into the system and adjusting its internal weights and parameters so it produces correct outputs on that data.
choices: Teaching a computer to speak
Adjust internal parameters to fit patterns in the data
Testing the system on new data
Installing software updates

exercises.question: What is a validation dataset used for?
exercises.answer: To check if the trained model works on data it has not seen
exercises.explain: A validation set is separate from the training set. It tests whether the model learned general patterns or just memorized the training data.
choices: To train the model
To check if the trained model works on data it has not seen
To fix bugs in the code
To store the results

exercises.question: If a model works perfectly on training data but poorly on new data, what likely happened?
exercises.answer: The model overfit by memorizing training data instead of learning patterns
exercises.explain: This is overfitting. The model memorized specific examples instead of learning general rules. A validation set during training should catch this.
choices: The training data was too small
The model overfit by memorizing training data instead of learning patterns
Neural networks cannot work on new data
The computer ran out of memory

exercises.question: What is supervised learning?
exercises.answer: Learning from labeled examples with correct answers
exercises.explain: In supervised learning, the training data includes both inputs and correct outputs. The system learns to map inputs to outputs.
choices: Learning without any data
Learning from labeled examples with correct answers
Having a human watch the system train
Learning only from images

exercises.question: What is unsupervised learning?
exercises.answer: Finding patterns in data without labeled correct answers
exercises.explain: Unsupervised learning finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data. Examples include clustering similar items or finding correlations without being told what to look for.
choices: Learning with a teacher
Finding patterns in data without labeled correct answers
Training on labeled data only
A type of supervised learning

exercises.question: What is reinforcement learning?
exercises.answer: Learning through trial and error with rewards and penalties
exercises.explain: Reinforcement learning trains a system by giving it rewards for good actions and penalties for bad ones. It learns to maximize total reward over time.
choices: The same as supervised learning
Learning through trial and error with rewards and penalties
Learning from historical data only
A type of unsupervised learning

exercises.question: Which type of learning would you use to teach a system to play a game?
exercises.answer: Reinforcement learning, with wins as rewards
exercises.explain: Reinforcement learning is ideal for games. The system learns which actions lead to winning and maximizes its score through trial and error.
choices: Supervised learning with all possible moves
Reinforcement learning, with wins as rewards
Unsupervised learning without any feedback
Only pre-programmed rules

exercises.question: What is overfitting and why is it a problem?
exercises.answer: Model learns noise in training data instead of true patterns
exercises.explain: Overfitting means the model fits the training data too closely, including random noise. It performs well on training data but fails on new data.
choices: Using too much training data
Model learns noise in training data instead of true patterns
The model not learning enough
Having too many computers

units.title: Neural Networks
units.tip: Neural networks are layers of artificial neurons connected together. Each neuron has weights that are adjusted during training. Backpropagation calculates how to adjust weights to reduce errors. Gradient descent is the algorithm that guides these adjustments step by step.

exercises.question: What is an artificial neuron?
exercises.answer: A basic unit that takes inputs, applies weights, and produces output
exercises.explain: An artificial neuron is inspired by biological neurons. It takes multiple inputs, multiplies them by weights, sums them, and applies an activation function.
choices: A biological brain cell
A basic unit that takes inputs, applies weights, and produces output
A type of algorithm
A processor in a computer

exercises.question: What are weights in a neural network?
exercises.answer: Parameters that determine how much each input influences the output
exercises.explain: Weights control the strength of connections between neurons. Training adjusts these weights to make the network produce correct outputs.
choices: The amount of data the network processes
Parameters that determine how much each input influences the output
How heavy a neural network file is
The number of layers

exercises.question: What is a layer in a neural network?
exercises.answer: A group of neurons that process the same type of information
exercises.explain: Layers are arranged sequentially. Input layers receive data, hidden layers process it, and output layers produce the final result.
choices: A physical piece of hardware
A group of neurons that process the same type of information
A saved checkpoint of the network
A type of learning algorithm

exercises.question: What does an activation function do in a neuron?
exercises.answer: Decides whether the neuron should activate based on its input
exercises.explain: Activation functions introduce non-linearity. They decide whether a neuron fires and how much. Common ones include ReLU and sigmoid.
choices: It multiplies the weights
Decides whether the neuron should activate based on its input
It calculates the error
It stores the training data

exercises.question: Why are multiple layers needed instead of just one?
exercises.answer: Multiple layers can learn complex, hierarchical patterns
exercises.explain: A single layer can only learn linear relationships. Multiple layers (deep networks) can learn non-linear, complex patterns in data.
choices: Because one layer is always too slow
Multiple layers can learn complex, hierarchical patterns
Because each layer adds different data
They are just used to make the network bigger

exercises.question: What is backpropagation?
exercises.answer: An algorithm that calculates errors backwards through the network to adjust weights
exercises.explain: Backpropagation computes how much each weight contributed to the error, then adjusts all weights to reduce that error.
choices: Moving data backwards through the network
An algorithm that calculates errors backwards through the network to adjust weights
A way to test the network on new data
Erasing the network and starting over

exercises.question: What is gradient descent?
exercises.answer: An optimization algorithm that adjusts weights to minimize error
exercises.explain: Gradient descent calculates which direction to adjust weights to reduce error, then takes small steps in that direction repeatedly.
choices: A slope in terrain
An optimization algorithm that adjusts weights to minimize error
A way to descend from space
A type of network layer

exercises.question: What is a loss function?
exercises.answer: A measure of how wrong the network's output is compared to the correct answer
exercises.explain: The loss function quantifies the error. Backpropagation and gradient descent work to minimize this loss.
choices: The amount of data lost in training
A measure of how wrong the network's output is compared to the correct answer
A function that removes data
The number of failed training attempts

exercises.question: What is a learning rate in gradient descent?
exercises.answer: How big each step is when adjusting weights
exercises.explain: The learning rate controls step size. Too small: training is slow. Too large: you might miss the best solution.
choices: How fast the computer runs
How big each step is when adjusting weights
The number of training examples
How many layers the network has

exercises.question: Why might a neural network get stuck at a local minimum instead of finding the global best solution?
exercises.answer: The optimization landscape has many valleys, not just one lowest point
exercises.explain: Gradient descent can find a nearby valley (local minimum) that is not the absolute lowest point (global minimum). This is a known challenge in deep learning.
choices: Because the computer does not have enough memory
The optimization landscape has many valleys, not just one lowest point
Because the network is too small
Because training data contains errors

units.title: Language Models
units.tip: Language models predict the next word in a sequence by understanding patterns in text. Tokens are small pieces of text (words or subwords). Transformers use attention to focus on important words. The context window is how much text the model can see at once.

exercises.question: What is a token in language processing?
exercises.answer: A small piece of text, like a word or subword
exercises.explain: Language models break text into tokens before processing. A token might be a whole word like 'hello' or part of a word like 'ing' in 'running'.
choices: A coin used in games
A small piece of text, like a word or subword
A type of grammar rule
A saved password

exercises.question: What is a transformer in AI?
exercises.answer: A neural network architecture that uses attention to process text efficiently
exercises.explain: Transformers process all tokens in parallel using attention mechanisms. They can handle long sequences and have become the standard for language models.
choices: A device that converts electricity
A neural network architecture that uses attention to process text efficiently
A type of programming language
A method to compress text

exercises.question: What does the attention mechanism do?
exercises.answer: Determines which words are most important for understanding context
exercises.explain: Attention weights each word based on its relevance. This lets the model focus on key words rather than treating all words equally.
choices: It pays the developer salary
Determines which words are most important for understanding context
It removes stop words from text
It translates text to another language

exercises.question: What is the context window of a language model?
exercises.answer: The maximum amount of text the model can see when predicting the next word
exercises.explain: The context window is a limit on how much prior text influences the next prediction. Larger windows allow the model to remember more context.
choices: The window of a computer monitor
The maximum amount of text the model can see when predicting the next word
How long it takes to train the model
The size of the training data

exercises.question: How do language models generate text?
exercises.answer: By predicting the most likely next token repeatedly
exercises.explain: Language models generate text one token at a time, using previously generated tokens as context to predict the next one.
choices: By copying text from training data
By predicting the most likely next token repeatedly
By asking a human what to write
By flipping a coin for each word

exercises.question: What is a hallucination in a language model?
exercises.answer: When the model generates false information presented as fact
exercises.explain: Hallucinations occur when language models produce plausible-sounding but incorrect information. The model is predicting likely text, not verifying truth.
choices: When the model sees images
When the model generates false information presented as fact
A type of training data
An error in the code

exercises.question: Why might a language model hallucinate?
exercises.answer: It predicts likely words without checking if they are true
exercises.explain: A language model is trained to predict the next likely word, not to check facts. On its own it has no way to tell a true sentence from a plausible false one.
choices: Because the hardware is broken
It predicts likely words without checking if they are true
Because the training data is too large
Because humans told it to lie

exercises.question: What is a prompt in the context of language models?
exercises.answer: The text input that the model uses to generate a response
exercises.explain: A prompt is the starting text or question. The model generates a continuation based on the prompt and its learned patterns.
choices: A reminder to the user
The text input that the model uses to generate a response
A saved section of code
A type of error message

exercises.question: How does temperature affect a language model's output?
exercises.answer: Higher temperature makes predictions more random; lower makes them more predictable
exercises.explain: Temperature is a parameter that controls randomness. A higher value (like 0.9) increases creativity but reduces consistency. A lower value (like 0.1) produces more predictable text.
choices: It controls the physical heat of the computer
Higher temperature makes predictions more random; lower makes them more predictable
It adjusts the size of the model
It determines the training data used

exercises.question: Why do language models sometimes repeat themselves?
exercises.answer: The model can get stuck in patterns it learned from training data
exercises.explain: Repetition happens when the model learns and reproduces patterns from training data, especially if those patterns are common in the data.
choices: Because they are broken
The model can get stuck in patterns it learned from training data
Because the user is forcing it
Because all language models must repeat

units.title: Using AI Well
units.tip: Effective use of AI means understanding what it can and cannot do. Know the strengths (pattern recognition, speed, scale) and limits (no true understanding, bias, hallucination). Verification of AI outputs is essential. Good prompts are specific and clear.

exercises.question: What makes a good prompt for an AI system?
exercises.answer: Clear, specific, and provides necessary context
exercises.explain: Good prompts tell the AI exactly what you want, include relevant background, and specify the format of the desired response.
choices: A single word
Clear, specific, and provides necessary context
As long as possible
Vague to test the AI's intuition

exercises.question: How can you improve an AI response that is not quite right?
exercises.answer: Refine the prompt with more specific instructions or examples
exercises.explain: If the first response is off, provide more detail, examples, or constraints. Iterating with better prompts usually yields better results.
choices: Always accept the first response
Refine the prompt with more specific instructions or examples
The AI is never wrong
Switch to a different AI system

exercises.question: What is the purpose of giving an AI system examples in a prompt?
exercises.answer: To show the format and style you want in the response
exercises.explain: Examples (few-shot prompting) help the AI understand the expected output format and tone by demonstration rather than just description.
choices: To slow down the AI
To show the format and style you want in the response
To waste tokens
To confuse the system

exercises.question: When should you use AI to help with a task?
exercises.answer: When it excels at the pattern-recognition or scale needed
exercises.explain: AI shines at finding patterns in large data, generating text, and processing at scale. Use it for those. Avoid it for tasks needing real-time verification or legal certainty.
choices: For every task
When it excels at the pattern-recognition or scale needed
Never, humans are always better
Only when the AI is free

exercises.question: What should you do before relying on an AI's answer for something important?
exercises.answer: Verify the output with a trusted source
exercises.explain: AI can hallucinate or misunderstand. Critical decisions require verification. Check facts, ask domain experts, or use multiple sources.
choices: Assume it is always correct
Verify the output with a trusted source
Flip a coin to decide
Ask another AI

exercises.question: What are AI systems good at?
exercises.answer: Pattern recognition, generating text, processing large amounts of data
exercises.explain: AI excels at finding patterns humans might miss and processing scale. It can generate fluent text and autocomplete ideas quickly.
choices: Understanding human emotions perfectly
Pattern recognition, generating text, processing large amounts of data
Replacing human judgment entirely
Knowing the future

exercises.question: What are AI systems not good at?
exercises.answer: Verifying truth, understanding context deeply, moral judgment
exercises.explain: AI lacks true understanding, cannot verify facts independently, and cannot make ethical decisions. It predicts plausible text, not truth.
choices: Speed
Verifying truth, understanding context deeply, moral judgment
Analyzing data
Following instructions

exercises.question: How should AI be used as a tool?
exercises.answer: As a starting point that humans then review and refine
exercises.explain: AI works best as an augmentation tool. Generate a first draft, then a human reviews, edits, and verifies the output.
choices: As a replacement for human work completely
As a starting point that humans then review and refine
Only when AI is 100 percent accurate
Never with human involvement

exercises.question: What responsibility do users have when using AI?
exercises.answer: To verify outputs, understand limitations, and use it ethically
exercises.explain: Users must verify AI responses before sharing them, understand AI cannot always be trusted, and avoid using it to deceive.
choices: No responsibility, AI is always right
To verify outputs, understand limitations, and use it ethically
Only to follow the AI's suggestions
To blame the AI if something goes wrong

exercises.question: How might AI amplify human biases?
exercises.answer: Training data contains real-world bias, and the AI learns and reproduces it
exercises.explain: AI systems learn patterns from training data. If that data reflects human bias, the AI will too. Bias in training data leads to bias in the model.
choices: AI is completely fair and unbiased
Training data contains real-world bias, and the AI learns and reproduces it
Only when humans tell it to be biased
AI cannot amplify anything

units.title: Safety and Ethics
units.tip: AI systems can reflect human biases from their training data. Privacy concerns arise when training on sensitive information. Misuse happens when AI is used to deceive or harm. Alignment means building AI that behaves the way humans intend.

exercises.question: What is bias in an AI system?
exercises.answer: When the system treats different groups unfairly due to training data
exercises.explain: Bias occurs when an AI system's training data overrepresents or underrepresents certain groups. This leads to unfair predictions for those groups.
choices: When the AI is very fast
When the system treats different groups unfairly due to training data
When humans disagree with the AI
A type of neural network

exercises.question: How can bias in AI systems cause real-world harm?
exercises.answer: Biased AI can deny loans, hiring, or services to unfairly treated groups
exercises.explain: When AI makes decisions (hiring, loans, parole), bias can perpetuate discrimination. A biased AI loan system might deny credit to certain groups unfairly.
choices: It cannot cause real-world harm
Biased AI can deny loans, hiring, or services to unfairly treated groups
Only in science fiction
Only if the AI is broken

exercises.question: What is privacy concern with AI?
exercises.answer: AI systems may memorize and leak sensitive information from training data
exercises.explain: If AI is trained on personal data, it might memorize and later reproduce sensitive information like addresses, emails, or health data.
choices: AI cannot access any data
AI systems may memorize and leak sensitive information from training data
Privacy only matters for passwords
All AI is completely private

exercises.question: How could AI be misused to deceive people?
exercises.answer: Generate fake content, deepfakes, or manipulative text at scale
exercises.explain: AI can generate text, images, and audio that are hard to distinguish from real. Bad actors might use AI to create misinformation or fraud.
choices: It cannot be misused
Generate fake content, deepfakes, or manipulative text at scale
Only for entertainment
AI prevents all deception

exercises.question: What is the problem with using AI for high-stakes decisions without human oversight?
exercises.answer: AI can make mistakes or exhibit bias that humans need to catch
exercises.explain: AI should not make final decisions in critical areas (parole, medicine, hiring) without human review. Humans can catch biases and errors.
choices: There is no problem
AI can make mistakes or exhibit bias that humans need to catch
Humans are always wrong
AI is always right

exercises.question: What is AI alignment?
exercises.answer: Building AI systems that behave the way humans intend
exercises.explain: Alignment means ensuring AI follows human values and instructions. Misaligned AI might pursue its goal in harmful or unintended ways.
choices: Lining up computers in a row
Building AI systems that behave the way humans intend
A type of neural network
Decorating an office

exercises.question: How can developers reduce bias in AI systems?
exercises.answer: Use diverse, representative training data and audit for fairness
exercises.explain: Reducing bias requires diverse training data, testing on different groups, and continuous auditing. No single step eliminates bias completely.
choices: You cannot reduce bias
Use diverse, representative training data and audit for fairness
Bias is good
Ignore the problem

exercises.question: What should companies do before deploying AI that affects people?
exercises.answer: Test for bias, get expert review, and monitor for harms
exercises.explain: Responsible AI deployment requires testing, expert oversight, and ongoing monitoring to catch bias and unintended harms.
choices: Deploy immediately without testing
Test for bias, get expert review, and monitor for harms
Never deploy AI
Only test on one person

exercises.question: Why is transparency important in AI systems?
exercises.answer: People affected by AI decisions should understand how they were made
exercises.explain: Transparency lets people understand, challenge, and appeal AI decisions. A black-box AI system is hard to trust or fix.
choices: It is not important
People affected by AI decisions should understand how they were made
AI should always be secret
Transparency makes AI slower

exercises.question: What is the responsibility of AI developers toward society?
exercises.answer: Consider harms, biases, and misuse potential before releasing
exercises.explain: Developers have a duty to anticipate harms, test safety, disclose limitations, and design with ethics in mind.
choices: No responsibility
Consider harms, biases, and misuse potential before releasing
Only to make profit
To ignore safety concerns
